contract.goal: every reconciliation run that acquires its lease is a recorded, readable resource with a real lifecycle; operator-triggered runs, dry runs and backfills are asynchronous with a per-run status resource; run history is retained for a bounded period, as specified in specs/reconciliation-admin
contract.output: 0015-create-run.sql; SyncRun entity/repository; RunRecorder wired into TaskRunner; TaskRunner.start + manual-run executor (429 on rejection); controller returning the run envelope; GET runs and runs/{runId}; RunPurge (retention + abandoned runs); JdbcRunLockIT cross-thread case; README EN+RU
constraints: the run lease is taken on the request thread, so 409 stays synchronous
telemetry (the run row) never fails a pass
enumeration runs are out of scope

decisions: 1.1: 0015-create-run.sql (sync_run; indexes (task_name, submitted_at DESC, id DESC) and partial (finished_at)); git add -N so check_migrations sees it (103 changesets conforming). SyncRun extends JpaBaseEntity<UUID> (assigned id = the lease's runId). NO status column: status is derived at the admin edge from started_at, finished_at and the existing RunOutcome, because web-core (OperationStatus) is an optional dependency the engine must not use, and a domain status enum would restate the operation vocabulary. Counts: demanded, fetched, produced - quarantined dropped: there is no quarantined inbox status, and in staged mode records are applied after the run, so no reliable per-run count exists. SyncRunRepository + QueryDSL fragment (keyset page, two-step bounded purge under the lock, abandon UPDATE). Module tests 302/302.

1.2: RunRecorder (engine; every write REQUIRES_NEW via TransactionTemplate; swallow-and-meter via new default ReconciliationMetrics.recordRunRecordFailed, Micrometer counter reconciliation.run.record.failed) wired into TaskRunner: run() records SCHEDULED, started on lease acquisition and finished in the existing finally with RunFailureCodes (run-failed for any exception, run-timed-out for TIMED_OUT). The design's 'the exception class's code' was dropped: the engine cannot see web-core's LocalizedException codes. RunViewsTest 3/3 covers the run-to-envelope mapping.

2.x (scope decisions, delta spec to be adjusted): (a) POST /runs becomes a recorded asynchronous run for a dry run and for a manual run of a key-addressed task; an enumeration walk and an ASYNC_JOB task's submit pass are not TaskRunner runs with a lease of their own, so they stay synchronous, answer 200 with the pass result, and record no run - ReconciliationAdminIntegrationTest's enumeration case was updated to 200 accordingly. (b) 429 carries retryAfterSeconds=30 as a problem property, not a Retry-After header: the problem pipeline renders exceptions and offers no header hook (export's 429 is the precedent), and an @ControllerAdvice is forbidden. (c) The public synchronous TaskRunner.dryRun/backfill were replaced by start(...) (+ private holding variants); ReconciliationIntegrationTest's four dry-run/backfill tests now start a run and wait for its row, asserting the same facts. (d) Architecture rules forbid entities in web signatures and treat web-package helpers as controllers, so the service returns RunSnapshot and RunViews lives in admin.service. Module 302/302 after these.

2.1-4.1: TaskRunner.start takes the lease on the request thread, records PENDING, hands the lease to reconciliationManualRunExecutor (ThreadPoolTaskExecutor core=max=runs.manual-concurrency, queue 0); on TaskRejectedException it discards the row, closes the lease and throws ManualRunCapacityException, mapped by the admin service to 429 manual-run-capacity with retryAfterSeconds. Controller: POST runs/backfills -> 202 + Location /runs/{id}; GET runs (keyset submitted_at,id; tier; status derived from timestamps+outcome) and GET runs/{id} via OperationResponses.poll (Retry-After 5s while non-terminal). RunPurge (lock ludwig-reconciliation-run-purge, runs.purge-interval) ends unfinished runs older than the task's run-timeout + 5 min as FAILURE/run-abandoned (instead of the design's lease-row check: the lease TTL IS the run timeout, and this needs no access to job-core's table), then purges finished runs past runs.retention in bounded batches. Bundle keys EN+RU: run-not-found, manual-run-capacity, run-failed, run-timed-out, run-abandoned; key-set parity ok.

Tests: ReconciliationRunHistoryIntegrationTest 8/8 (manual run 202 + Location, polled to SUCCEEDED with counts 1/1/1 and result href; 409 while the lease is held elsewhere, no row; scheduled partner-catalogue failure listed under status=FAILED with run-failed; dry run report as result with nothing staged; backfill result requested/staged; run.started/run.finished audit events carry runId and correlation id; keyset paging; 31-day-old run purged (404) and an hour-old unfinished run ended run-abandoned). ManualRunCapacityTest 2/2 (rejection releases the lease and discards the row; held lease -> empty, nothing recorded). RUN_TIMED_OUT is covered by RunViewsTest only: a real 5-minute timeout is not practical in an IT. The admin-level 429 translation has no test of its own.
5.1: JdbcRunLockIT.releaseFromAnotherThread (lease taken on the test thread, closed on another, then claimable by a second replica). JdbcRunLockIT 9/9.

Delta spec corrected to the built behaviour (spec follows code): enumeration and ASYNC_JOB submit passes stay synchronous 200 and unrecorded (new scenario); 429 carries retryAfterSeconds, not Retry-After; the accepted envelope is 'that run's envelope' (the worker may already have moved it past PENDING when the row is read back); counts are demanded/fetched/produced; non-terminal run resources carry Retry-After; abandoned runs are ended by the purge (new scenario). openspec validate --strict: valid.

6.1: README EN+RU: runs in the read row of the Administration table, a 'Runs are resources' paragraph, a ludwig.reconciliation.runs.* table, runbook action rows (run/dry run/backfill now asynchronous; runs listing) and two situation rows (stuck RUNNING, 429). Heading counts match; check_image_pins rc=0. Follow-ups: run-history item now names what stays open (enumeration and async-job runs).
